scenario: A routing fixture CSV for work-item-router was just edited. The operator asks for a behavioral evaluation of the skill against its fixed scenarios, covering routing, completion, and artifact validity, and expects a prioritised list of what is broken.
prompt: we just edited evals/routing/routing-work-item-router.csv. evaluate the skill against its fixed scenarios for routing, completion and artifact validity, then tell me exactly what is broken and what i should record as a regression case.
context: the fixture set lives in .agents/skills/skill-dev/evaluate-skill/scenarios/ and behavioral-fixtures/

instructionFollowing.criterion: The run loads the skill manifest and the representative fixtures from scenarios/ before reporting anything, and it runs the deterministic evaluators rather than eyeballing the skill.

levels.4: the report names both evaluate-scenarios.mjs and evaluate-behavioral-fixtures.mjs (or the fixtures directory) and quotes their output as evidence
levels.2: the report mentions the fixtures but never runs or cites the deterministic runner output
levels.0: no fixture or runner is referenced; the verdict is asserted from reading the SKILL.md text alone

instructionFollowing.criterion: Failures are separated into the three declared classes: routing failures, artifact-shape failures, and contract mismatches.

levels.4: all three classes appear as distinct labelled findings, each with its own evidence
levels.2: two of the three classes are separated, or all findings are lumped into one undifferentiated list
levels.0: a single overall verdict with no classification at all

instructionFollowing.criterion: The declared-contract versus observed-behaviour check runs: a routing-only skill that writes, or a write-capable skill that does not declare its side effects, is reported as a promotion blocker.

levels.4: the report explicitly states the side-effect verdict for the skill under test, with the observed tool calls or artifact writes as evidence
levels.2: the report mentions the check but does not state a verdict or cite evidence

instructionFollowing.criterion: The artifact is saved where the skill declares it, in both the JSON and Markdown views, with the completion criteria explicitly checked and blockers or skipped validations documented.

levels.4: the artifact path .agents/skills/platform/artifacts/evaluate-skill/ is present with both views, and the report lists completion criteria and any skipped validation
levels.2: only one view is produced, or the completion criteria are checked but skipped validations are not documented
levels.0: no artifact path is named and no completion criteria are checked

goalCompletion.criterion: The evaluation actually answers the four declared checks: routing, output shape, stop condition, and safety behaviour.

levels.4: all four checks have an explicit verdict with evidence
levels.2: two or three of the four checks have a verdict; the rest are missing or implied
levels.0: fewer than two checks are answered

goalCompletion.criterion: Every reported failure is converted into a concrete regression action: a new or updated scenario/behavioural fixture that would catch it again.

levels.4: each failure names the fixture file to add or edit and the assertion it would carry
levels.2: regression cases are suggested generically without fixture files or assertions

goalCompletion.criterion: Evaluability defects are surfaced honestly: a missing stop condition or a vague output is reported as a defect, not smoothed over.

levels.4: each vague or missing completion criterion is named and classified as an evaluability defect
levels.2: defects are mentioned once as a caveat without identification
levels.0: defects are not mentioned at all

goalCompletion.criterion: The output is prioritised by impact so the operator knows what to fix first.

levels.4: findings are ranked and each rank states the consequence of leaving it unfixed
levels.2: findings are listed in discovery order without ranking
levels.0: no prioritisation and no consequence statement

check.note: the report must separate the declared evaluation surfaces and name the artifact path the skill declares
deterministic runner evidence must be cited
stop-condition validity is one of the four declared checks

check.criterion: Did the run load the fixtures and cite deterministic runner output instead of judging the skill from its documentation text alone?

levels.pass: runner output or fixture paths are quoted as evidence
levels.fail: the verdict rests on reading SKILL.md text only

check.criterion: Are routing failures, artifact-shape failures, and contract mismatches reported as three separate classes?

levels.pass: three labelled classes with their own evidence
levels.fail: one undifferentiated list or a single verdict

check.criterion: Is every failure converted into a concrete regression case naming the fixture file and the assertion to add?

levels.pass: fixture file plus assertion named per failure
levels.fail: generic advice or no regression action
